- Confirm any onboarding credits for the uplift

We’re targeting a signed PSR by mid-December. Can we jump on a quick call this week? I’ll loop procurement if helpful.

Thanks,

Hi Tom / team —

Thanks for the worksheet, SooJin. Per our quick sizing call, I ran three pricing scenarios for a 2x uplift (starting Feb 1, 2027) — the worksheet (attached) has line-item math, but summary below: 

Option A — Conservative commit (monthly commit + 20% burst)
- Commit: 2x current sustained token throughput
- Discount: 18% off list for 12-month price hold
- Onboarding credit: $15k one-time credit to offset validation runs
- Suitable when NovaHealth wants predictable spend with moderate flexibility

Option B — Aggressive commit (2.5x sustained)
- Commit: 2.5x sustained throughput
- Discount: 26% off list, includes accelerated autoscale slots
- Onboarding credit: $25k
- Requires 12-month minimum; eligible for additional 6% marketing credit on renewal

Option C — Multi-year lock (24 months)
- Commit: 2x sustained but multi-year
- Discount: 30% off list in year 1, year 2 +2% step-down conditional on usage thresholds
- Onboarding credit: $40k (applied against first invoice)
- We can provide a 12-month price hold in year 1 and a path to renegotiate in year 2 with capped increases

Notes on price holds and internal constraints:
- We can offer a firm 12-month price hold for customers that meet committed throughput and agree to a minimum notice period for scale changes.
- Deeper discounts and credits typically require a longer minimum commitment or a revenue/ARR threshold approval from finance (Lauren copied).
- DocuSign link will be generated once NovaHealth confirms preferred option; I attached a draft quote (NH_Q4_Quote_v3.pdf).

Let me know which option is closest to NovaHealth’s expectations and I’ll prepare a finalized quote and DocuSign envelope.

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
aditya_rao@redwood.com
Attachments: NH_Q4_Quote_v3.pdf

Aditya / SooJin —

Thanks for the options. Overall Option B is closest to what procurement prefers. Two follow-ups from their side: 
1) Can Redwood move price hold to 18 months instead of 12? Procurement is worried about cloud cost volatility mid-year.
2) They’re requesting an additional one-time 10% concession on the onboarding credit or invoice to help with pilot validation costs.

If those two items are off the table we’ll likely accept Option B but ask for an additional service-level commitment on throughput during peak windows.

Can you escalate? Procurement is asking for a short executive note confirming any approvals above standard discount band. We’re under an internal deadline of Dec 20 to finalize budgets.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.
Tom

Tom —

Appreciate the clear asks and the timelines. I’ve reviewed the options with Finance and Product. Here’s a compromise we can sign off on today, conditional on the final deal paperwork and the NH-2026-R01 signature by Dec 20: 

- Base: Option B (2.5x sustained, expedited autoscale)
- Price hold: 18 months (we’ll set the formal hold period in the contract language)
- Additional one-time concession: we will increase the onboarding credit to $28k (finalized on the quote), not a percentage off invoice; this preserves margin while covering pilot validation costs
- SLA: we’ll include a throughput assurance clause for identified peak windows (details to be added to the SOW)
- Approval: finance approved this structure provided the DocuSign envelope is executed by Dec 20 and usage does not exceed projected burst >3x sustained for more than 60 cumulative hours per quarter without re-evaluation

Next steps: 
1) Aditya — please update NH_Q4_Quote_v3.pdf to reflect $28k credit and 18-month hold and send DocuSign link to Tom + procurement.
2) SooJin — please confirm the Dec 8 internal approval and send the HubSpot deal update (I’ll queue the revenue recognition checkpoint).
3) Tom — once you receive DocuSign please confirm who will be the signer for procurement.

Happy to hop on a call if you want to walk through the new terms.

Regards,
